what_it_does: This paper explores whether activation functions—the mathematical operations that add non-linearity to neural networks and enable them to learn complex patterns—can run at ultra-low numerical precision (fewer bits per number) without losing accuracy. Existing work has proven this works well for matrix multiply operations in neural networks, but activation functions have not been thoroughly tested. The work systematically measures accuracy loss when activation functions use 8-bit, 6-bit, 4-bit, 3-bit, and 2-bit representations.
